text.p: The chairman of the Maine Yankee nuclear power plant said he will make a "significant announcement" on Tuesday about the facility, which is shutdown for repairs and up for sale.
Officials declined to elaborate on the subject of the 4 p.m. EDT (2000 GMT) news conference, which will come after a board meeting at the 910-megawatt facility's corporate headquarters in Brunswick.

The Nuclear Regulatory Commission on Tuesday made public a list of equipment repairs and upgrades it will require before the 25-year-old plant in Wiscasset, Maine is allowed to restart. It has been shut since December 6, 1996.

"Fundamental change is required at Maine Yankee to assure past problems do not recur. Before startup, the staff expects the licensee to demonstrate that previous management weaknesses and flaws in problem identification and corrective action processes have been effectively addressed," the NRC told Maine Yankee.
Maine Yankee's board has been approached by Peco Energy Corp about a possible sale of the plant.

It is now 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co. and 10 percent by other New England utilities.

Maine Yankee has not operated at full power since early 1995, and a series of embarrassing safety and management problems prompted the NRC to place it on the Watch List of troubled plants needing closer inspection.
The board late last year approved $38 million in extra spending in 1997 to address safety problems and in February hired Entergy Corp to supervise management and the restart efforts.

The current shutdown was prompted by the discovery of misrouted electrical cables and logic problems in circuitry. The plant is also inspecting a $29 million repair made in 1995 on thousands of steam generator tubes.
The Justice Department is also reviewing an NRC investigation into charges Maine Yankee fraudulently manipulated safety testing used in the 1980s to win approval for a power increase.
